svg.title: Plain prediction against shift test-time augmentation
svg.desc: Two pages that flip. Page 1: a plain prediction runs the network once on the whole input image, which holds a person and a small dog, and returns a bounding box with a score for each: person 0.91 and dog 0.70, both kept. Page 2: with shift_tta=4 the same input is moved down and right by 0, a quarter, a half and three quarters of a patch on a canvas one patch larger, so nothing is cropped. Each snapshot goes through the same network once and returns its own boxes and scores. The network finds the person in every pass but misses the dog in one, so that pass counts as 0. The boxes are mapped back by subtracting each offset, grouped when they have the same class and an IoU above 0.6, and averaged into one box per object. In the combine panel the steps play in order: the boxes of each pass slide back by their offset, boxes of the same object are grouped, each group becomes one mean box, and its score is built from one quarter of every pass score, where a pass with no box adds nothing. The person gets 0.91 and the dog gets 0.54, and both are kept. Masks keep the pixels that at least half of the matched masks cover. Scores are illustrative.
svg.text: One input, shifted snapshots, combined predictions
Each snapshot is predicted once. The offsets are known, so the boxes are mapped back and combined. Scores are illustrative.

g.text: the whole input image as it is: one pass through the network
input image; the grid is the backbone patches
output: every box with its score
One pass gives one box and one score per object.
A score depends a little on where the object sits in the patch grid, and a small object can even be missed.
Next page: shift_tta predicts shifted snapshots of the same input and combines them.
the same input, moved down and right by 0, ¼, ½ and ¾ of a patch: four snapshots, four passes
page 2 of 2 (plain predict() gave person 0.91, dog 0.70)
one box per pass, best score first
3 box: mean of the group's boxes
(a pass with no box counts as 0)
5 keep if the mean score > threshold
6 mask: pixels in at least half
